claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered single-phase BCC solid solution.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The limited plasticity of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo results from its high Mo-induced electronegativity difference.
Replacing half of the Mo content with V gives NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5.
Partial replacement of Mo by V will reduce the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
V substitution will alter lattice distortion and local elastic stress fields in NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5.
V introduces atomic-spacing fluctuations and lattice distortion.
Atomic-spacing fluctuations introduced by V will modestly increase solid-solution strengthening in the modified alloy.
Partial replacement of Mo with V will reduce dislocation pinning and dislocation friction stress.
Partial replacement of Mo with V will lower the Peierls stress.
Lower dislocation friction will increase room-temperature compressive plasticity.
NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5 will have greater strain to fracture than equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo under room-temperature compression.
The compressive yield strength of NbZrTiHfMo0.5V0.5 will decrease only slightly from 1719 MPa and remain in a high-strength regime.
The beneficial strength-plasticity effect requires the modified alloy to remain a single-phase disordered BCC solid solution.
Excessive V substitution may cause phase separation or secondary-phase precipitation.
Phase separation or secondary-phase precipitation may negate strength retention or reduce overall mechanical performance.
A yield-strength decrease greater than approximately 10% relative to 1719 MPa would contradict the predicted strength retention.
Failure to obtain a statistically higher fracture strain in the modified alloy would contradict the predicted plasticity improvement.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says V substitution lowers lattice friction and Peierls stress, whereas record PMC10385466::web::014 reports that V-induced atomic-spacing fluctuations increase locally fluctuating Peierls potentials and friction stresses in CoCrNi alloys.

The claimed effect is explicitly conditional on retention of a single-phase BCC structure, yet observation of secondary phases is defined as falsification. Secondary phases would instead place the sample outside the stated applicability conditions unless phase retention itself is also an explicit prediction.
